draft.title: How reliable are DeepSeek R1 perplexity comparisons with only 8 blocks tested?
draft.body:
A perplexity test on DeepSeek R1 models ran on just 8 out of roughly 560 blocks, which the original tester warns should be taken with a massive grain of salt. Since the test sample is so small, it raises questions about how meaningful the perplexity differences really are between models with different expert counts.

Additionally, perplexity might not be a fair metric for chain-of-thought models because they don’t get to perform their reasoning steps during the test. This could skew comparisons if one model relies more on chain-of-thought mechanisms than another.

Given these limitations, how much confidence should we place in these perplexity results when deciding between DeepSeek R1 variants? Are there better or more practical ways to benchmark these models locally without exhaustive testing?
